answer.evidence: This is a flat floor decal of loose bricks, each only about 4 rows tall. The column scan shows the same pattern in every brick: a dark outline row, then one light row (#a35f4c or #b27361), then one darker row (#70402f), then an outline row. The silhouette widths run 3, 9, 11, 13, 8, 11, 9, 8, 12, 8, 2 with no single large body. Each brick has about a 1-row light top and a 1-row darker face. That is a rim-like strip, not an ellipse, a roof, or a front-edge line with eave shadow, and no part has a front face of 3 rows or more. The object reads as a flat top-down scatter of bricks, which fits the flat kind.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a tiny cluster of about 5 red-brown bricks, smaller than one 16x16 tile, on a blank background. The reference paving has 7 visible tones per tile and the grass 3, both with tufts and grain across the whole surface. Next to them the candidate looks thin, flat and sticker-like. Nothing is laid out as a continuous ground surface, so it does not meet the standard for this kind.
